record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Characterize the chiral maps that fail to be polyhedra, that is, the chiral maps that do not satisfy the abstract-polytope conditions needed to be rank-3 polytopes.

evidence.quote: Problem 18 Characterize chiral maps which are not polyhedra.

artifact.status_search_result: Web searches turn up surveys and a recent (2025) Cambridge monograph "Abstract Chiral Polytopes" by Pellicer–Weiss with an open-problems appendix, but no source clearly states that an intrinsic characterization of chiral maps that fail to be polyhedra has been obtained. The problem appears to remain unresolved in the literature, though no explicit "still open" claim was located.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems (Appendix C) - Abstract Chiral Polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Appendix C listing open problems on chiral polytopes in the 2025 Cambridge monograph.
status_evidence.claim: A current open-problems compendium on chiral polytopes exists, but no resolution of the specific characterization is reported here.
